title: Token Origins Waterfall UX Playbook
content:
Context and goal:

This is a working playbook for a token-level "waterfall" view that traces every output token back to its origin and cost path (model variant, KV-cache hit, batching decision, hardware tier). Primary goal: make it possible for an engineer or SRE to answer "Which tokens caused a spike in cost or latency for this invocation?" within 30s of opening the console. Secondary goals: provide clear remediation actions (model fallback, cache pin, prompt trim suggestions) and surface SLA-relevant evidence for post-incident review.

Why this is different than existing token breakdowns:
- Current token views summarize counts and cost buckets; they don’t link tokens to decision points (e.g., rerouter fallback, quantized variant used, cache hit/miss).
- We want an explicit provenance chain per token: input origin -> routing decision -> runtime variant -> hardware kernel -> token produced.

Constraints / non-goals:
- Not building a full forensic replay system (that lives in infra). This view will *reference* traces and cached artifacts, not re-run the inference.
- Not responsible for long-term storage; UX should surface links to trace logs and preserved payloads.

User journeys (top priority)
1) On-call triage: user sees a specific invocation with high 99th-latency. They filter to invocation and expand a token waterfall to see that tail tokens were produced after a fallback to CPU quantized model and a KV cache miss. Action: acknowledge, add ticket to pin CUDAs and enable cache warming.
2) Product cost review: product manager looks at a surge in token cost per-API route and wants to see whether costs are driven by increased prompt size or model variant change. Action: surface aggregated token origins (prompt vs. generated) and overlay model-variant timeline.
3) Developer prompt optimization: dev wants to see which tokens are repeated across invocations and could be cached. Action: group repeated token sequences and suggest prefix cache candidates.

Information architecture (high level)
- Header: invocation metadata (route, org, model pinned/variant, region, start/end timestamps, tokens generated, total cost, P50/P95/P99 latency).
- Left rail: token timeline (scrollable, compact tokens as colored chips grouped by segment).
- Main pane: waterfall lane per token group (input tokens, prompt context, model decisions, runtime variant, cost attribution).
- Right rail: quick actions and evidence (link to trace, trace snippets, links to ticket creator, suggested remediation).

Wireframe notes (sketch level)
- Token chip colors: input tokens (blue), cached tokens (green), generated tokens (orange), fallback-generated (red outline). Chips shrink at high density; hover reveals provenance tooltip.
- Waterfall lanes: each lane is a stacked horizontal bar: left edge = request start time, right edge = token emission time. Overlay markers for routing decisions (R), cache hit (H), batching pause (B).
- Breadcrumb view atop the pane showing the selected token's provenance tree (textual): "input[123] -> KVCache:miss -> Router:fallback->cpu-quantized-v2 -> kernel:triton-v2". Each element is clickable to reveal logs.
- Mini-heatmap below waterfall showing per-token cost and latency as dual bars (cost on left, latency on right) so you can scan for tokens with disproportionate cost vs time.

Interaction details
- Expand token group: click a chip to expand full per-token row with: token text, byte-size, token index, model used, kernel, cost cents, latency ms, related log snippets (first 300 chars), and link to full trace.
- Select multiple tokens to compare provenance side-by-side. Useful to confirm whether two costly tokens share a root cause (common reroute or same KV miss).
- Filter bar: filters by model variant, cache hit/miss, hardware (GPU/CPU), time-since-invocation (e.g., show only tokens after router fallback), cost threshold.
- Save view: save a filtered view as a named investigation so you can attach it to a Jira ticket.

Backlog / grooming items (prioritized)
- P0: Minimal provenance pipeline and UI: show 1) per-token cost + latency; 2) one-line provenance string; 3) links to trace. (est 3 sprints)
- P1: Token chips + waterfall UI with hover tooltips and heatmap; multi-select compare; save view. (est 3 sprints)
- P2: Auto-suggestions: detect repeated token sequences across invocation window and propose prefix cache candidates; auto-classify probable root cause (cache vs routing vs quantization) using heuristics. (est 2 sprints + offline classifier)
- P3: Integrations with rollouts: surface which rollout a token originated from (canary/primary) and overlay rollout timeline. (est 1 sprint)
- P4: Playback mode: lightweight replay of token emission timing for debugging (no model re-run, use recorded timing and logs). (est 2 sprints)

Acceptance criteria (for P0)
- Open an invocation and expand token waterfall; at least 80% of tokens show a provenance string and cost/latency values.
- Each provenance element links to a matching trace id / log snippet; clicking opens raw trace in new tab.
- Filter by cache hit/miss returns consistent set with infra's cache logs for the same invocation.

Open questions / risks
- Privacy: token text may contain PII. We need to minimize exposure by masking configurable parts by default. Proposal: mask tokens that match sensitive classes and require elevated permission to reveal.
- Data volume and UI performance when invocations generate 10k+ tokens. Strategy: pagination + density collapse + server-side summarization.
- Trace linking: need a reliable deterministic mapping from token id to trace shard; infra-team needs to provide a compact index service (INF-987).
- Cost attribution model disputes: accounting differences between infra billing and UI attribution may confuse customers; include a caveat and link to accounting doc.

Prototype notes and experiment ideas
- Start with a high-fidelity click-through built in Framer/FIGMA that uses anonymized real traces to validate density interactions.
- A/B test triage time metric: measure time-to-insight vs existing token summary. Target: 2x faster for triage tasks.
- Run a small onsite with 3 internal SREs to run 5 simulated incidents; capture missing artifacts and refine filters.

Suggested copy and microcopy (for UX)
- Token chip tooltip header: "Token #{{index}} — generated"
- Provenance breadcrumb: "Origin: {{input|prompt}} • Router: {{policy}} • Variant: {{model}} • Kernel: {{kernel}}"
- Right-rail action: "Create incident from view" -> prefill description with selected token indices and links.

Implementation notes for infra handoff
- Need an index endpoint: /v1/trace-index?invocation_id=xxx returning list of token ids, token timestamps, cost_usd_cents, latency_ms, model_variant_id, cache_hit_bool, routing_event_id. (Lightweight: <200KB per 1k tokens).
- Add a compact token text redaction flag per token to avoid pulling full token strings unless user is authorized.
- Synthetic example payload (for the proto): show a 120-token invocation with 10% cache hits and one fallback to cpu-quantized-v2 at token 86.

Notes to reviewers
- This doc is intentionally action-oriented; I want early engineering feedback on feasibility of the proposed index endpoint and rough performance constraints.
- Diego: can you confirm INF-987 scope? Also what is the max recommended payload size for a single UI API call from infra?
- Jin: rough sketch of color palette and chip states in Figma attached in linked_artifacts.

Next steps (immediate)
- Align with infra (INF-987) and serving-runtime owners to finalize minimal index schema (due EOW).
- Build a small mocked Framer prototype and schedule internal triage session (target: 2025-03-12).
- Groom P0 user stories and ship initial API contract to eng backlog.

Appendix: quick sketch (text-only)
[HEADER] Invocation: /chat/completion • org: Acme • model: redwood-13b • tokens: 120 • cost: $0.42 • P99: 1.18s
[LEFT RAIL] token chips: [prompt: "Hi"] [prompt: "Please summarize"] [generated: "Summary:"] ...
[WATERFALL]
- lane 1 (prompt) |----|
- lane 2 (router decisions)    R@0.12s -> fallback@0.86s
- lane 3 (generation) |---- token1(23ms,cost 0.001c) |---- token86(420ms,cost 0.03c) [red-outlined]
[RIGHT RAIL] Actions: "Open trace" "Create incident" "Save view"

End of playbook — comments encouraged.
